Hi Ari — thanks for the usage file, that helps. Below are three pragmatic paths we often recommend; I put the high-level economic impact next to each so procurement has something to review. Laura and Ben, looping you in for the legal/billing flow and discount bands.

Option A — Incremental top-up (pay-as-you-go with smoothing credit)
- Add a staged uplift bucket (monthly true-up) sized at +220% for next 6 months
- No change to contract term; billing is monthly based on true-up usage
- We provide a 6% usage credit applied on incremental token spend over baseline (applies only while uplift remains > baseline)
- Pros: minimal invoice shock; Cons: lower committed discount

Option B — Staged committed uplift + partial annualization
- Commit to 60% of the expected uplift as a short-term add-on for remaining term
- We annualize only the committed portion, invoice as 3 equal installments over the next 3 months
- Discount band: 12% on the committed uplift tranche; remainder billed overage
- Pros: better unit economics; Cons: some upfront invoice commitment

Option C — Temporary bridge voucher + co-term amendment
- Issue a bridge voucher (one-time credit) to smooth invoices for the next 3 months while you finalize a co-term amendment
- If you co-term within 60 days, voucher converts to a portion of committed capacity credited to new term
- Voucher value example: $45k credit based on projected usage delta (convertible)
- Pros: minimizes accounting churn; Cons: requires amendment to lock long-term pricing

Fallback / downgrade: all three options include a 30-day review window and a rollback clause where we reduce committed bands if trailing 90-day usage falls below 70% of uplift; any converted vouchers that already turned into committed capacity would be prorated and returned as credit per Amendment terms.

Next steps: I attached a one-page with numbers (see Redwood_Uplift_Options_v2.pdf). Ben — can you confirm how we would show the voucher conversion on the invoice and whether we need a single amendment or two docs? Laura — what timeline for a simple co-term amendment (proc/legal review) if they choose Option C?

Cheers,
Jonas Weber

Jonas / Laura — quick notes from billing ops:
- Voucher conversion: we post a credit memo when voucher is issued; if converted, we apply it as a prepayment allocation against the new committed invoice (so it doesn't double-count)
- For Option B, we can do three equal invoices labeled as "Committed Add-on — Installment X" to keep finance happy
- Amendment docs: a single amendment that references the new committed capacity + a short SOW appendix is ideal; DocuSign ready.

Also recommend adding a 90-day consumption checkpoint and an SLA note for priority queueing during the uplift window — simple line item, low friction.

Ben Carter
